title: Opaque Authorization Bypasses via Verbose Denial Explanations
pattern: Returning highly verbose error messages to unprivileged or unauthenticated users detailing the exact reasons, missing groups, or network rules causing an authorization denial.
why_bad: It exposes critical system topology details to attackers, who can use this detailed roadmap to target the precise directories, networks, or administrative users needed to bypass security.
detection: Format macros returning system constraints, database fields, or group requirements inside 403 Forbidden response handlers.
fix: Return generic, opaque "Access Denied" errors to the client; expose diagnostic details only through random support tokens analyzed in backend logging systems.
source: `Heather Adkins et al. - Building Secure and Reliable Systems (2020)`, Ch 5, p. 73.
